authored_from: Articles (Serious)/technical/3B1B — Monitor - Formal Execution.md, Additions — 'Frequency-domain change (harmonics)'
note: ★★ The payoff is SUPPRESSION and it must be honest: energy at a known period is an expected cycle, and the residual after removing the known cycles is the genuine-shift signal. A monthly bill arriving on schedule must not fire a 'spend is up' alarm — and the time-domain CUSUM, on the same series, does.

reconciliation_before_building.★★_the_MON_13_row_said_this_consumes_sig: Checked before building, and the premise does not hold. `signal.rs` is the **excitable-medium** primitive — `Phase`, `Pulse`, `Field`, refractoriness, a wave travelling across a **graph of nodes**. It produces no time series to transform. The confusion is traceable to the Additions paragraph itself, which runs two sentences together: the harmonics sentence, and then *'The Signal primitive Monitor relays is defined formally in §4B (§III)'* — a **cross-reference about where Signal is defined**, not a statement that harmonics consumes it. The row read the second sentence as a dependency of the first.
reconciliation_before_building.★_what_it_actually_reads: The article says *'the fold [...] over a windowed series'* — which is the **same `W = d(s,V)` series `detect.rs`'s EWMA and CUSUM already run over**, and which `MonitorEngine` already keeps a history of. So this takes a **supplied** `&[f64]` window, exactly as `criticality.rs` takes a supplied window rather than owning one. **No parallel windowing is defined**, which was the real substance of the instruction.
reconciliation_before_building.★★_and_TESTING_forced_a_correction_inspe: The first implementation attributed a known cycle to **one bin** and the on-schedule monthly bill came back a *genuine shift*. The reason is the row's own name: a bill is a periodic **impulse**, not a sinusoid, and an impulse train puts energy at **every multiple of its fundamental**. Attributing only the fundamental leaves the harmonics in the residual. Fixed by attributing the harmonic series `k, 2k, 3k, …` — and the cost is named where it lives rather than discovered later: **a genuine shift landing exactly on a harmonic of a known cycle is absorbed with it.** That is inherent, not a defect — you cannot both explain a non-sinusoidal cycle and keep its harmonic bins free.

divergence.statement: `dft`, `fourier`, `fft`, `harmonic`, `spectral`, `seasonal` and `periodic` are all grep-0 in apps/api/sustena/ — seven clean zeros. Nothing anywhere reads a series in the frequency domain, so nothing can tell a season from a shift.
divergence.★_the_counterweight_the_SUBSTRATE_is_at_: Two halves. **The substrate:** the time-domain detectors ship — `detect.rs`'s EWMA and CUSUM over `W = d(s,V)`, held per-sustain by `MonitorEngine`, which already keeps the very history this transforms. So MON-13 is not waiting on an input; it is the **frequency-domain complement** of a chain that already runs. **And the need is real, not hypothetical:** the household genuinely has monthly rhythms — `budget.allocate` carries a `period: "monthly"` param, `budget.record_income` a `frequency: "monthly"`, and the advisory rule proposes `period: "monthly"` allocations. A monthly bill landing in a spend series is exactly the thing a time-domain detector fires on, and today nothing would stop it.
divergence.★★_and_the_case_is_PROVEN_rather_than_ar: The conformance case runs the **real `Cusum`** from `detect.rs` over the same series the frequency-domain reading calls an expected cycle, and asserts it **fires**. So *'the time-domain detectors cannot do this alone'* is a measured fact about this codebase's own detector rather than a claim about detectors in general.

term_by_term.★ a windowed series to read: AT PARITY as a substrate — `MonitorEngine` keeps per-sustain histories, and `detect.rs` consumes exactly this series.
term_by_term.the Monitor→Controller escalation bounda: AT PARITY — and reused rather than duplicated: a genuine shift is classified with `detect::classify`, the same `excess → Severity` table.
term_by_term.★★ a frequency-domain reading: RUST-AHEAD. Seven grep-0 terms; there is no transform under any other name.
term_by_term.★★ cycle-vs-shift suppression: RUST-AHEAD, and this is the row. Today a monthly bill would false-alarm — the CUSUM case proves it on this side, and nothing on the other side is shaped differently.
term_by_term.★ declared periods to use as known cycle: PARTLY AT PARITY, and in a way worth naming — `period: 'monthly'` is a **free-text label** on a pocket, not an interval anything expands. EVT-11 makes it a real recurrence here, which is why `KnownCycle::from_periods` exists.
term_by_term.an FFT: NEITHER SIDE, AND DELIBERATELY. A direct O(N²) DFT is honest at household-scale windows and needs no dependency; the FFT is a **scaling slot**, named rather than pulled in.

the_greppable_false_positives_named_so_n.frequency (19 hits, none a spectrum): ★ Every one is `budget.record_income`'s `frequency` **param** — the free-text string `'once'` / `'monthly'` describing how often an income arrives. Genuinely adjacent in meaning and completely unrelated in kind: a label on a transaction, not a component of a series.
the_greppable_false_positives_named_so_n.cycle (15 hits, none periodic): `import cycle`, `council cycle`, `max_steps (safety guard against cycles)` — a graph cycle, a governance round and a module-load cycle. None is a rhythm.
the_greppable_false_positives_named_so_n.dft / fourier / fft / harmonic / spectra: Seven clean zeros. No transform under another name.

divergence.what_python_does_have_and_why_it_is_not_: The series, the detectors that run over it, the escalation path they cross, and free-text labels that name the very rhythms this would use. What it does not have is any way to look at the series' periodicity — so the monthly bill it already knows about by name is invisible to the detector that fires on it.
divergence.the_honest_limits: Six. (1) ★★ A SHIFT ON A HARMONIC OF A KNOWN CYCLE IS ABSORBED — attributing `k, 2k, 3k, …` is what makes a non-sinusoidal cycle explainable at all, and the price is that a genuine shift landing exactly on one of those bins is suppressed with it. Inherent, not a defect, and stated where the attribution happens. (2) ★ NO WINDOWING OF ITS OWN — the window is supplied, so window length and sample interval are the caller's choices and they change what is resolvable; that is deliberate (`criticality.rs` does the same) but it means a badly-chosen window degrades the reading silently. (3) ★ THE MEAN IS REMOVED, A LINEAR TREND IS NOT — removing a trend is a modelling choice, and doing it silently would suppress exactly the slow drift a Monitor most wants to see. (4) O(N²) — honest at household scale, and **an FFT is a named scaling slot** rather than a dependency taken now. (5) SPECTRAL LEAKAGE IS NOT WINDOWED AWAY — a period that does not divide the window smears across neighbouring bins; no Hann/Hamming taper is applied, because a taper is another declared choice and its absence is more legible than a silent one. (6) NOT WIRED INTO `MonitorEngine` — like MON-8's tracker, this is designed to sit alongside the chain and the wiring is named rather than claimed.
divergence.when_python_catches_up: These cases become parity vectors unchanged. The first step is not the transform — it is EVT-11: turning `period: 'monthly'` from a label into a real recurrence gives the known cycle something to be derived from.
divergence.not_a_divergence_in: R1 behaviour. Purely additive: a new module, no call site in `execute` or `MonitorEngine`, no change to `detect.rs` beyond reusing its `classify`, and no existing vector touched.

fixture.why: The household case the Additions names: weekly samples of a spend series with a bill arriving on a monthly rhythm. 32 samples with a spike every 4 gives 8 full cycles — enough to be a rhythm rather than a coincidence.

transform_cases.name: a_pure_sinusoid_puts_its_power_in_its_own_bin
transform_cases.why: The transform checked against a case with a known answer before anything is built on it — four cycles across the window land in bin 4, at period 8 samples, with the amplitude recovered to 1.0. A DFT that is wrong here is wrong everywhere downstream.

transform_cases.name: ★_the_MEAN_is_removed_so_a_LEVEL_is_not_read_as_a_RHYTHM
transform_cases.why: ★ A constant series has no rhythm, and must read as having none. Without removing the mean, a household's average spend would dominate every reading and the residual would be a statement about how much they spend rather than about whether the pattern changed.

transform_cases.name: a_window_too_short_or_not_finite_is_refused
transform_cases.why: Two samples have no frequency content to read, and a NaN anywhere makes the whole transform meaningless. Both are named errors rather than a zero-filled spectrum, because a spectrum of zeros reads as *nothing is happening*.

suppression_cases.name: ★★_a_monthly_bill_arriving_ON_SCHEDULE_is_an_EXPECTED_CYCLE
suppression_cases.why: ★★ THE ROW'S PAYOFF. The bill lands every 4 samples for 8 cycles; its energy — fundamental **and harmonics** — is attributed to the declared monthly cycle, the residual is small, and **nothing escalates**. The season arrived, as seasons do.

suppression_cases.name: ★★_the_TIME_DOMAIN_detector_WOULD_HAVE_FIRED_on_exactly_that_series
suppression_cases.why: ★★ The claim *'this is what the time-domain detectors cannot do alone'* made a **measured fact about this codebase's own detector** rather than an assertion about detectors in general. The real `Cusum` from `detect.rs`, with a declared `μ₀`/`δ`/`h`, walks the same series and crosses `h` — because a spike is a spike to an accumulator. The frequency-domain reading, on the identical data, says expected cycle. **Complement, not veto.**

suppression_cases.name: ★★_the_SAME_MAGNITUDE_arriving_OFF_CYCLE_is_a_GENUINE_SHIFT
suppression_cases.why: ★★ The other half of the proof, and the one that stops suppression from being a blanket mute. Same spike, same size, at a period the declared cycle does not explain — so it stays in the residual and surfaces, at a severity from the same table any other alert uses. A suppressor that could not do this would be an off switch.

suppression_cases.name: ★_a_NEW_rhythm_ON_TOP_of_a_known_one_still_surfaces
suppression_cases.why: ★ The realistic case rather than the clean one: the monthly bill is **still arriving** and something else has started. The known cycle is explained and the new one is not, so it surfaces — which is what makes this useful in a household that never stops having a monthly bill.

honesty_cases.name: ★★_a_period_the_WINDOW_CANNOT_RESOLVE_is_INDETERMINATE_not_expected
honesty_cases.why: ★★ THE HONESTY POINT, and the trap the brief names. The cycle is **declared** — fully authorised — but a 12-sample window cannot carry a 10-sample period: fewer than two full cycles fit, so it is indistinguishable from a trend. Subtracting energy at a bin the window cannot resolve would **remove a real shift under the name of a season**. ★ Declaration authorises a cycle; it does not make a short window able to measure it. Those are two different requirements and both are needed.

honesty_cases.name: ★★_an_UNESTABLISHED_cycle_cannot_suppress_and_SAYS_WHY
honesty_cases.why: ★★ The other half: seen once is not a season. Using it to suppress would hide a shift behind a rhythm **nobody has confirmed** — the exact dishonesty this codebase refuses everywhere else. The refusal names the count it saw and the count it needed, because a caller told only *no* cannot tell an unlucky window from a wrong declaration.

honesty_cases.name: ★_the_SAME_cycle_ESTABLISHED_enough_times_DOES_suppress
honesty_cases.why: ★ The pair to the case above, and the reason it is not simply strictness: the difference between the two is **the evidence, and nothing else**. Same series, same period, same threshold — one refuses and one suppresses, because one has been seen 8 times and the other once.

honesty_cases.name: ★_INDETERMINATE_is_neither_of_the_other_two_answers
honesty_cases.why: ★ It does not escalate (nothing has been shown) and it is not an expected cycle (nothing has been explained). The same third-answer family as `Skew::Unknown` and `Soundness::Unavailable` — *we cannot yet tell* is a real answer, and collapsing it into either neighbour is how a system becomes confidently wrong.

policy_cases.name: a_nonsense_policy_is_refused_at_declaration
policy_cases.why: A residual threshold outside 0..=1 is not a fraction; a period of 1 sample is not a period; and `min_cycles_to_establish < 2` would let a single occurrence establish a season, which is the whole thing the establishment rule exists to prevent.

policy_cases.name: ★_a_cycle_derived_from_a_REAL_EVT_11_recurrence_matches_its_period
policy_cases.why: ★ The tie-in the brief asks for, run against a real `Recurrence`: a declared monthly budget period **is** a declared cycle. `FREQ=MONTHLY;BYMONTHDAY=1` expanded from 1 January, sampled daily, gives a 31-sample cycle — the actual length of that month, not an averaged 30.4, because EVT-11 expands real periods rather than a nominal one.

policy_cases.name: a_cycle_from_EVT_11_periods_needs_at_least_TWO_of_them
policy_cases.why: One period gives a span, not a recurrence — there is no second boundary to measure a repeat against. Refused by name rather than assuming the span is the cycle.

policy_cases.name: two_cycles_landing_in_ONE_BIN_cannot_double_count_its_power
policy_cases.why: Two declared cycles whose periods round to the same bin must not let the explained power exceed the total — an accounting error there would let a spec suppress arbitrarily much by declaring the same rhythm twice.
